narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Slightly cooler and windier than yesterday; cloud little changed. Showery from the afternoon, with thunder possible from the morning, peaking tomorrow afternoon. 30°C / 86°F high, 19°C / 67°F low. Sky mostly cloudy early as reported, mostly cloudy at midday and mostly cloudy in the evening. Wind SW at midday; gusts to 44 km/h (24 kt). UV index 8.5 (very high). Air quality 43 (good) at Dunga Beach, the highest of 3 stations. As of 06:01, reports through 05:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 23°C / 73°F; low so far 21°C / 70°F; peak sustained 7 km/h; sky mostly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS show temperatures and winds much the same through Friday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Wednesday will be Mostly cloudy with high 28–30 °C, low 19 °C, gusts to 30 km/h (16 kt) and rain 2.1–9.4 mm. Thursday remains Mostly cloudy, high 28–32 °C, low 19 °C, gusts to 27 km/h (14 kt) and rain 4.4–21.4 mm. Friday stays Mostly cloudy, high 27–30 °C, low 19 °C, gusts to 30 km/h (16 kt) and rain 8.1–29.3 mm. The record line notes Best Match as the best rain record for Day+3.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values exceed the thunderstorm threshold, with Best Match, ECMWF, ICON and UKMO all above the limit and a peak at 11:00. Thunder possible from the morning, peaking tomorrow afternoon. Sudden gusts could far exceed the forecast wind, reaching well above 44 km/h (24 kt). No specific bulletin warning was issued by the Kenya Meteorological Department.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Winam Gulf wind will be northeasterly overnight at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 11 km/h (6 kt), then southwesterly by midday at 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 19 km/h (10 kt), and into the evening at 16 km/h (8 kt) gusting 28 km/h (15 kt). Peak gust on the Gulf is 34 km/h (18 kt). Thunderstorm gust hazard is present as thunder is possible.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1009 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1015 hPa) — a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the south-southeast. Pressure overhead is near-steady. BASIN PRESSURE: today’s mean sea-level pressure sits between 1013.1 and 1015.1 hPa. The pressure trend is +1.1 hPa, indicating a slight rise.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

REVIEW indicates that at Day+0 no model is meaningfully better than the others, though GFS slightly over-forecasts cloud cover and daytime highs, and ECMWF slightly under-forecasts daytime highs and peak wind. Best Match under-forecasts peak wind. The call’s rain probability (100%) aligns with the models, but Best Match’s rain record is slightly low. KMD’s forecast matches the call on temperature but provides fewer details on wind and rain. DATA SUFFICIENCY notes 57 checks for Day+0, a settled picture despite uneven coverage, and 23 checks for Day+3, sufficient for model comparison.
